overview: ChatGPT ads expand to 89 countries, targeting users on free plans while keeping paid tiers ad‑free.
OpenAI models become directly purchasable on Google Cloud, pairing frontier AI with enterprise data controls.
Meta issues non‑voting shares to fund AI projects, while competitors launch new agents and self‑improving models.

top.title: ChatGPT Ads expands to 26 new countries as over 100,000 advertisers have used the platform
top.summary: OpenAI adds ChatGPT Ads to 26 more countries, reaching 89 total. Ads appear only on free/Go plans, are labeled, and do not influence answers, aiming to fund free access while protecting user privacy.

top.title: OpenAI models are coming to Google Cloud
top.summary: OpenAI partners with Google Cloud to list its frontier models and Codex in the Model Garden, enabling enterprise customers to buy and run them with Google’s governance and infrastructure.

top.title: Meta to create a new class of shares to fund AI push
top.summary: Meta will issue a new class of non‑voting shares to raise capital for AI development, acquisitions, and employee compensation, supporting its expanding AI agent portfolio.

top.title: Recursive launches Flint, a laptop coding model it says was largely built by AI
top.summary: Recursive releases Flint, a 40‑billion‑parameter coding model that runs on laptops, built largely by its AI‑driven Eureka Machine, demonstrating early self‑improving AI research.

top.title: Anthropic takes on Muse with Claude Duet, its new AI agent
top.summary: Anthropic unveils Claude Duet, an AI agent for professionals that integrates with apps, offers task automation, and includes safety checks for sensitive data, available as a research preview.

top.title: OpenAI CLI
top.summary: OpenAI publishes an official CLI for its REST API, supporting Go 1.26+, offering command auto‑completion, update checks, and detailed help without requiring an API key for basic usage.
